defects_found.note: Two instances of the word 'beno' (his son) in the row's own prose carry niqqud but no cantillation and do not byte/NFD-match any actual oshb token (every real occurrence of the word carries a trope mark). Confirmed as the only two genuine Hebrew-collation defects across all 322 Hebrew runs in rows 1-50 by running the campaign's own normalize_hebrew_in_json.py (dry-run) over the row set: ok=315, mention=6, defects=2 (both this pair). The fully-troped forms of the same word are quoted correctly elsewhere in the same field. Non-blocking: used as a lexical label after the evidentiary quote was already given correctly, not as a freestanding evidentiary claim.

Three WEB-attributed quotes deviate from the verbatim WEB text in non-substantive ways: two are sentence-initial capitalization changes made to embed the quote mid-sentence (row 004: 'these are the sons of Ishmael,' for WEB's 'These are the sons of Ishmael.'; 'all these were the sons of Keturah,' for WEB's 'All these were...'), and one (row 007) is a deliberately ellipsis-compressed refrain ('Bela died, and ... reigned in his place,') representing a formula that recurs verse after verse with different names, not a claimed verbatim quote of any single verse. None misrepresent the underlying WEB wording.

Row 004 names v.5 and v.8 as register-head labels for comparison, and lists a six-member chapter-wide elleh-occurrence set (1.23,29,31,33,43,54) in prose, but boundary_evidence_refs does not mirror v.5, v.8, v.43, or v.54 (v.23/29/31/33 are present via other citations). Row 025 makes a categorical claim about 'every intervening conjunctive fragment since v.11' (i.e. 4.12-4.20, the preceding row's own span) without individually citing those verses, though the anchor verse 4.11 is present in refs. In both cases the underlying textual claims were independently verified as accurate by direct sweep of 1Chr_oshb.txt; this is a citation-completeness gap, not a substantive evidentiary error, and contrasts with the fuller ref-mirroring practice seen elsewhere in this batch (e.g. decision 027's ten-verse sweep, fully mirrored into refs).

Row 046 states the Shuppim/Shapham consonants recur at 5.12 and 26.16 beyond the row's own 7.12/7.15. An independent full-book sweep found one further occurrence the row did not name: 27.27 (ha-Shifmi, 'the Shiphmite', a gentilic epithet). This does not change the row's own conclusion -- the row uses the recurrence to argue these consonants are common and non-diagnostic for the Ir/Aher identity question, and a third unrelated occurrence only reinforces that point.

defects_found.description: Several WEB-tagged English quotations render the source's typographic (curly) apostrophe as a plain ASCII apostrophe -- e.g. "fathers' households" for WEB's "fathers’ households", "wife's name" for "wife’s name", "God's house" for "God’s house". Every instance checked is otherwise byte-exact once apostrophe style is normalized (confirmed programmatically against 1Chr_web_clean.txt for all affected quotes), and several are legitimately elided with a disclosed "..." for a verse's middle portion, which also checks out fragment-by-fragment. Content is not altered or paraphrased; this is a keyboard-typography substitution, not a fidelity problem, and does not affect any boundary argument.

The WEB-tagged quotation "These are the names of the children whom he had in Jerusalem." closes with a period, but WEB 14:4 actually continues past that point with a colon introducing the name list ("...in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,"). The row silently substitutes a period for WEB's colon at its own truncation point rather than eliding with "..." as done elsewhere in this batch. The list-head argument itself is unaffected -- the opening clause quoted is accurate -- but the closing punctuation of the tagged WEB quote is invented rather than sourced.

A recurring, non-blocking class across this block (matching the campaign's largest defect class from the peer round, per CYCLE_STATE Phase 6): comparanda argued in prose, or interior verses of a row's own span that are directly discussed or Hebrew-quoted, are not individually mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs even though byte-verified accurate. Most instances are light structural comparanda (e.g. 051 and 071 citing 7:1/7:6/8:1 as tribal-register-opener analogues; 055 arguing a closing formula's reach back to 8:1/7:6). Two instances are more substantive: 094's entire closing argument turns on a directly-quoted two-word Hebrew skeleton at 16:8 (independently verified here as the book's only other occurrence of that exact phrase besides 16:34, which IS in refs) with no 16:8 ref at all; 092 argues that v7's date formula points back to v1 (outside the row's own span) to explain why it does not bind v7, but 16:1 is not in refs either. In every case the row's own boundary still rests on its own cited evidence; these are supplementary comparanda, not the argument's foundation. (Distinguished during review from several look-alike, non-defective patterns that were NOT counted here: rejected-alternative sentences that merely name a rival span's boundaries e.g. 8:29, 11:1-9, WEB 12:15, v.15, v1-3 without arguing their content; blanket same-span negative-scope claims over an already-large row e.g. 071's "vv26-47"; back-references to a neighboring row's already-established span with its own bookend verses already cited e.g. 087's vv5-10, 097's vv37-42; and citations of book_strategy_draft.md's own classification list in 084, which cites the strategy document rather than arguing the verses' content directly.)

defects_found.location: M8-1Chr-076, boundary_rationale, NOTE FOR BOSS sentence
defects_found.description: The row's own disclosed calibration-disparity note reads "this row holds high confidence on the same seam that 077 treats as live and holds at medium", but the row's own confidence field is medium, not high. Per CYCLE_STATE Phase 9c the boss ratified a 076 high→medium delta applied at finalize as a disclosed orchestrator field-level operation; the confidence field itself is correctly medium and matches 077's medium grade on the same seam (the calibration disparity the note originally flagged is in fact now resolved), but the explanatory sentence inside boundary_rationale was not back-patched to match and still describes the row as holding its pre-delta high grade. Non-blocking: span and evidentiary argument are unaffected, and the field value is correct; only the embedded prose is stale.

defects_found.note: The row's own text states that 'the chamat here is the object complementizer completing the verb of hearing... not a causal connector, the same construction correctly labeled at 19.6's parallel ki (M8-1Chr-104)'. Chamat (Het-Mem-Tav) is the place name 'Hamath' in 'Tou king of Hamath', not a complementizer; the actual complementizer in the same quoted clause is the word immediately following it, ki. This looks like a word-identification slip rather than an error of interpretation -- the surrounding argument (that the clause is a 'that'-complement of hearing, paralleling decision 104's reading of 19.6's ki, not a causal 'because') is itself sound and the boundary conclusion for 18.1-18.13 does not depend on which specific word is named. Correctable without reopening the row's disposition.

The WEB-tagged citation of 17.16 renders 'and he said, Who am I, Yahweh' as one continuously quoted clause. WEB's own text has an internal opening quotation mark before 'Who' (narration followed by nested direct speech) that the row's single pair of quotation marks flattens, and the citation stops short of WEB's own continuation ('...Yahweh God, and what is my house...') without an ellipsis marking the truncation. All quoted words remain in WEB's exact order with nothing paraphrased, added, or reordered; this is a typographic/truncation-marking gap, not a content misrepresentation.

Four rows quote or rely on specific Hebrew wording from a named comparandum verse outside their own span without adding that verse to boundary_evidence_refs, though the immediate neighbor verses used alongside it usually are present: decision 103 quotes 18.2's vayakh as part of its nakah-chain description (18.1 and 18.3 are in refs, 18.2 is not); decision 104 names 18.1 as sharing 'the same campaign-report device' as its own 19.1 opener; decision 116 compares the cantillation of 21.9's lemor against its own 22.8's lemor at the diacritic level; decision 126 checks its own disclosure of a WEB harmonization at 24.23 against 23.19's actual MT wording. Every underlying textual claim in all four cases was independently verified as accurate by direct comparison against 1Chr_oshb.txt and 1Chr_web_clean.txt; this is a reference-list completeness gap, not an evidentiary error, and matches the class already logged for rows 004 and 025 in postcheck_part1.json.

Decision 136 cites 27.31 (both web: and oshb: refs) as a comparandum for its own closing-formula pattern, but does not repeat the verified clause-level WEB/MT divergence at 27.30/31 that the immediately preceding sibling row, decision 135, discloses in full. The specific content decision 136 draws on from 27.31 -- the 'these were the rulers of the property' closing formula -- is present in both witnesses and is not the part of the verse affected by the divergence (the Jaziz-the-Hagrite clause WEB moves into v.30), so no argued claim in decision 136 is actually put at risk; flagged per the standing instruction that this divergence remain disclosed wherever either verse is cited.
